model_family: Whirlpool WTW5057LW 4.7 cu. ft. top-load washer
sticker_location: Beneath the washer lid on the tub rim. Lift the lid and look around the edge of the tub opening.

parts.label: Lid
parts.where: The big cover on top that lifts up to reach the clothes.

parts.label: Lid lock
parts.where: The small latch under the edge of the lid opening, where the lid meets the washer body.

parts.label: Model and serial tag
parts.where: Under the lid, on the rim around the tub opening.

parts.label: Wash basket
parts.where: The large round drum inside the washer that holds the clothes.

parts.label: Removable agitator
parts.where: The tall center post in the middle of the tub on agitator models. It lifts out for bulky loads.

parts.label: Impeller plate
parts.where: The low, flat turning plate in the center bottom of the tub on impeller models instead of a tall post.

parts.label: Built-in water faucet
parts.where: The small spout at the back inside top of the tub. Its button is on the back control panel.

parts.label: Bleach dispenser cup
parts.where: The small marked cup in the top rim inside the tub for liquid bleach only.

parts.label: Cycle knob
parts.where: The big turning knob on the raised back panel. Turn it to pick a wash cycle.

parts.label: Settings knob
parts.where: The smaller knob next to the big cycle knob on the back panel, for water level or other choices on some models.

parts.label: Power button
parts.where: The Power button on the back control panel, near the cycle knob.

parts.label: Start/Pause button
parts.where: The Start/Pause button on the back control panel. Hold it to start a cycle.

parts.label: Drain hose
parts.where: The gray ribbed hose at the back that carries dirty water to the sink or drain pipe.

parts.label: Water inlet hoses
parts.where: The pair of hoses at the back that bring hot and cold water from the wall taps to the washer.

parts.label: Inlet valve screens
parts.where: Tiny screens just inside the hose connections on the back of the washer, where the water hoses screw on.

parts.label: Leveling feet
parts.where: The four small screw feet at the bottom corners of the washer that touch the floor.

parts.label: Power cord
parts.where: The plug and cord coming from the back of the washer to the wall outlet.

symptoms: I press start and nothing happens
The washer will not start
No lights or no sound when I try to start it

plan.diagnosis: The lid may not be fully latched, or the control may need a simple reset. The washer will not run until the lid is closed and Start is held.
safety: Do not reach inside if the tub is moving.
Unplug the washer before checking the cord or outlet.

steps.instruction: Close the lid until it clicks shut.
details: Move clothes away from the lid edge.
The lid should sit flat all around.
steps.check: The lid sits flat and closed.

steps.instruction: Press and hold Start for three seconds.
details: A short press may not start it.
Watch for a light or a sound.
steps.check: Lights come on or the washer starts filling.

steps.instruction: Unplug the washer from the wall outlet.
details: Pull the plug, not the cord.
steps.check: The plug is fully out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Wait five minutes with the washer unplugged.
details: This lets the control reset.
steps.check: Five full minutes have passed.

steps.instruction: Plug the washer back in firmly.
details: Use a grounded three-prong outlet.
Do not use an extension cord.
steps.check: The plug is pushed in all the way.

steps.instruction: Press Power, then hold Start again.
details: Close the lid first if it opened.
steps.check: The washer lights up and begins the cycle.

symptoms: There is water left in the tub
Clothes are soaking wet at the end
It will not drain or spin

plan.diagnosis: A kinked drain hose or an uneven, tightly packed load often stops draining and spinning. Too much soap can also slow the spin.
safety: Unplug the washer before moving hoses.
Wipe up spilled water to avoid slipping.

steps.instruction: Look behind washer at gray drain hose.
details: Find it at the back of the washer.
It goes to a sink or drain pipe.
steps.check: You can see the full drain hose behind the washer.

steps.instruction: Straighten any bends or kinks in hose.
details: Water must flow freely through it.
Clear anything blocking the sink drain.
steps.check: The hose runs smoothly with no sharp bends.

steps.instruction: Push hose only four inches into drain pipe.
details: No more than about 4.5 inches inside.
Do not tape over the drain opening.
steps.check: Only a short end of hose is in the pipe.

steps.instruction: Spread wet clothes evenly around tub wall.
details: Drop clothes in loose piles, not one lump.
Take some out if the tub looks stuffed.
steps.check: Clothes sit evenly around the tub wall.

steps.instruction: Turn knob to Drain and Spin.
details: Use Rinse and Spin if that is listed instead.
steps.check: The knob points to Drain and Spin.

steps.instruction: Press and hold Start for three seconds.
details: Close the lid before starting.
steps.check: Water drains out and the tub spins.

problems.cause: a kinked drain hose or lopsided load

symptoms: It shakes and bangs during spin
The washer walks across the floor
It is very loud when spinning

plan.diagnosis: Clothes bunched on one side make the tub thump and shake. A washer that rocks on its feet will shake even more.
safety: Stop the cycle and wait until the tub stops.
Do not reach in while the tub is moving.

steps.instruction: Press Pause and wait until tub stops.
details: Wait until all movement and sound stop.
steps.check: The tub is completely still.

steps.instruction: Open lid and spread clothes around wall.
details: Untangle sheets and towels first.
Drop items in loose, even piles.
steps.check: Clothes are spread evenly, not in one lump.

steps.instruction: Remove a few items if tub looks stuffed.
details: A very full tub may not spin well.
Wash heavy blankets separately.
steps.check: The load looks loose, not packed tight.

steps.instruction: Rock washer gently from opposite front corners.
details: Push one corner, then the other.
All four feet should touch the floor.
steps.check: You can tell if the washer rocks or sits firm.

steps.instruction: Twist the wobbly foot down until firm.
details: Turn it until that corner stops rocking.
Use a wrench on the lock nut if needed.
steps.check: The washer no longer rocks corner to corner.

steps.instruction: Turn knob to Rinse and Spin.
details: Close the lid, then hold Start.
steps.check: The washer spins smoothly without banging.

symptoms: No water is going in
It takes forever to fill
It fills and drains at the same time

plan.diagnosis: Both wall taps must be on and the hoses must not be kinked. Tiny screens where the hoses join the washer can get clogged with grit.
safety: Turn both water taps off before unscrewing hoses.
Unplug the washer before working behind it.
Stop and call for help if you see a leak you cannot stop.

steps.instruction: Turn both wall water taps fully on.
details: Both hot and cold taps must be open.
They are on the wall behind the washer.
steps.check: Both wall taps are fully open.

steps.instruction: Straighten any kinks in water inlet hoses.
details: Follow each hose from wall to washer.
Move the washer slightly if a hose is pinched.
steps.check: Both hoses run smoothly with no sharp bends.

steps.instruction: Turn off both wall water taps.
details: Turn them the other way until water stops.
steps.check: Both wall taps are off.

steps.instruction: Unscrew one inlet hose behind the washer.
details: Hold a bucket under it for drips.
Use pliers gently only if hand-tight will not move.
steps.check: The hose end is free and over the bucket.

steps.instruction: Brush the tiny screen inside hose opening.
details: Use an old soft toothbrush with mild soap.
Do not pull the screen out.
steps.check: The small screen looks clear, with no grit.

steps.instruction: Screw hose back on by hand.
details: Make it snug, but do not force it.
Repeat for the other hose if needed.
steps.check: The hose is snug and straight.

steps.instruction: Turn taps on and check for leaks.
details: Dry the fittings, then feel for drips.
Turn taps off at once if it leaks.
steps.check: Fittings stay dry with taps on.

symptoms: The lid lock light keeps flashing
It says the lid will not lock
It will not spin because the lid is open

plan.diagnosis: Clothes tucked under the lid or soap crust around the latch can stop the lid from locking. Clearing the edge and resetting often helps.
safety: Do not force the lid down.
If the lock looks cracked or broken, stop and call for service.

steps.instruction: Press Pause and wait until tub stops.
details: Wait until all movement stops.
steps.check: The tub is completely still.

steps.instruction: Lift lid and move clothes away from edges.
details: Check all around under the lid.
Push bulky items down into the tub.
steps.check: Nothing is caught under the lid edge.

steps.instruction: Wipe white crust from around lid lock.
details: Use a soft, damp cloth.
Clean where the lid meets the body.
steps.check: The latch area looks clean and clear.

steps.instruction: Close the lid until it clicks shut.
details: Press down gently at the front edge.
steps.check: The lid sits flat and closed.

steps.instruction: Unplug the washer from the wall outlet.
details: Leave it unplugged for five minutes.
This resets the control.
steps.check: The plug is out and five minutes pass.

steps.instruction: Plug washer back in after five minutes.
details: Then close the lid again.
steps.check: The plug is firmly in the outlet.

steps.instruction: Press and hold Start for three seconds.
details: Listen for the lid locking click.
steps.check: The lid locks and the cycle starts.

symptoms: The washer smells musty
Clothes do not smell fresh after washing
There is gunk around the lid

plan.diagnosis: Soap and dirt build up inside the tub over time, especially with too much soap. A monthly Clean Washer cycle clears the build-up.
safety: Do not mix bleach with other cleaners.
Keep cleaner tablets away from children and pets.

steps.instruction: Take all clothes out of the tub.
details: Check for socks stuck around the center post.
steps.check: The tub is completely empty.

steps.instruction: Put one cleaning tablet in tub bottom.
details: Put it in the tub, not any cup.
Do not add soap or other cleaners.
steps.check: One tablet sits at the bottom of the tub.

steps.instruction: Wipe gunk from around lid and bleach cup.
details: Use a soft, damp cloth.
Dry with a towel when clean.
steps.check: The rim and cup look clean.

steps.instruction: Close the lid until it clicks shut.
steps.check: The lid sits flat and closed.

steps.instruction: Turn knob to Clean Washer cycle.
details: If there is no Clean Washer, check the cycle guide online.
Use the cleaning cycle it lists.
steps.check: The knob points to the cleaning cycle.

steps.instruction: Press and hold Start for three seconds.
details: Let the cycle run without stopping it.
steps.check: The cleaning cycle starts and runs.

steps.instruction: Leave lid open after cycle ends.
details: This helps the tub dry out.
Leave it open between washes too.
steps.check: The lid stays open and the tub can dry.

symptoms: Still full of water after fixing the hose and load
It hums but no water goes out

plan.diagnosis: With the hose straight and the load even, the drain pump is probably blocked by a sock or a coin, or has failed. On this washer the pump sits behind the cabinet, so it's a job for a pro.
replacement_parts: Drain pump for your model (match it by the model number)

steps.instruction: Unplug the washer
steps.check: The plug is out.

steps.instruction: Bail out the water with a bucket
details: Wring the clothes out and set them aside.
steps.check: The tub is mostly empty.

steps.instruction: Find the model number under the lid
details: Lift the lid and look at the back edge of the opening.
steps.check: You have a photo of the tag.

steps.instruction: Call a pro, or order the part for your model
details: Tell them what you already tried, so you don't pay for the same checks.
A parts store can match the part to your model number.

plan.aftercare: Use a mesh bag for socks and small things so they can't reach the pump.

problems.cause: a blocked or failed drain pump

parts.label: Top and raised back control panel — see-through
Impeller plate — flat plate under the agitator base
Drain hose — gray ribbed hose at the back
Water inlet hoses — hot and cold pair at the back
Inlet valve screens — inside the rear hose connections
Leveling feet — four screw feet at the bottom corners
